ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The graph of the line $l_{1}\colon y=k_{1}x+b$ and the line $l_{2}\colon y=k_{2}x$ in the same Cartesian coordinate system are shown in the figure. The line $l_{1}\colon y=k_{1}x+b$ intersects the x-axis at the point $(-3, 0)$. What is the solution set of the inequality in terms of x, $k_{2}x<k_{1}x+b<0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the graph, it is apparent that the intersection point of line $l_{1}$ and line $l_{2}$ is at ($-1$, $-2$), and within line $l_{1}$, $y$ decreases as $x$ increases.\\
Because $y=k_{1}x+b$ intersects the $x$-axis at point ($-3$, $0$), and the solution set of the inequality $k_{2}x<k_{1}x+b$ with respect to $x$ is $x<-1$,\\
Therefore, the solution set for the inequality $k_{2}x<k_{1}x+b<0$ with respect to $x$ is $-3<x<-1$,\\
Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{-3<x<-1}$.
